title: Camellia Viaduct
description: An entirely chordal song unfolds above a seven-bar descent: C, B, B-flat, A, A-flat, G, G. Each return hears that descent in a different harmonic light. The C–E-flat–D–G refrain comes from Camellia Refractions; its last appearance leaves the ground and arrives in E-flat major.
difficulty: Advanced chordal passacaglia and chromatic voice leading
technical_note: The long bass fifths frame a melody in the tops of the RH chords. Give the seven-bar ground an unbroken direction. The opening chord melody returns in bar 15, while later chords change its path. Play all chord attacks together; the final bass departure is deliberate.

performance.note: Keep each chromatic descent connected while releasing pedal at the changing upper harmonies. The last seven bars gradually stop following the old ground.

composition_time_source: Recorded when the first score was saved.

audio_reverb.description: Subtle warm room; preserve the clarity of moving voices.
